findings.title: Early exit is lifted out of the A7 seam, so the "preserved" swap point can no longer deliver distance-ranked selection
findings.description: Plan 140 entry #10 says both interventions "use the `getNeighbors` seam already designed in slice 145 (A7)" and asks to "replace counter-gating in `get_neighbors_first_k` with a `break`". Option A instead leaves the seam's counter-gating intact and adds `if k_found >= max_neighbors: break` in the calling loop, *before* the seam is reached; line 112 then claims "A7 seam preserved". Once the break fires, no candidate after the k-th is ever passed to the seam — which is exactly what a distance-ranked (k-nearest) implementation needs in order to replace worse neighbors with closer ones. A future distance-ranked swap would have to remove or relocate the cap check in the tick-kernel body, defeating slice 145 A7's isolation guarantee, and it leaves duplicate/dead cap logic in both caller and seam. Specify a seam-owned "stop scanning" predicate (or a strategy flag) so the seam stays the single place neighbor selection is decided, or explicitly downgrade the A7 claim here and in the plan.

findings.title: The `break` does not terminate the cell scan, and the candidate-count model contradicts slice 148's measurements
findings.description: The `break` is placed in the innermost `for kk in range(start, end)` loop (lines 29–31, 38–44). That exits only one cell's slot loop; the enclosing `for drow` / `for dcol` loops still iterate over all (2S+1)² cells, so at S=3 all 49 cells are visited and each re-enters the `kk` loop to re-check the cap. No cell-loop-level `scan_done` gate is specified. Line 58's "With S=3 alone: candidates loaded drops to ~5000" and "With both: candidates loaded ~555" also contradict the 148 Phase 2 rediagnosis the doc cites as its basis (`49 cells × 555 ≈ 27,000`, "still better than 45,000"), and "compose multiplicatively" does not follow from a 45,000→27,000 pre-cap reduction plus a cap at 32. A2's ≥5× `force_total` gate is justified by these numbers, so the model needs correcting and cell-loop termination needs stating (a light `done` flag suffices — no new mechanism).

findings.title: `cell_size = query_radius / S` does not say which radius, leaving the neighborhood-preservation claim unproven for multi-profile workloads
findings.description: Slice 145's fused tick derives one global `cell_size` from `max_query_radius` across all profiles while the kernel reads `query_radius` per agent from the profile table; the (2S+1)² scan covers every profile's radius only if S is applied to the largest one. Lines 53 and 80 say "cell_size = query_radius / S" and "only the cell_size value changes" without naming `max_query_radius`, and line 56 asserts "correct neighborhood is preserved" without qualification. With a mixed-radius workload a smaller-derived cell_size silently drops in-radius neighbors — a gap A4's 20% statistical-parity gate would not necessarily catch. Name the invariant (`cell_size = max_query_radius / S`) and state explicitly what happens when a valid S makes `grid_w × grid_h` exceed the existing setup-time cell cap, rather than leaving that failure implicit.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough is written against a bench CLI the harness does not provide
findings.description: Every gate command in Steps 2/3/5 invokes `python scripts/bench.py --backend ... --config ... --N ... --ticks ... --subdivision-factor ... --parity-check numpy`. Slice 141 defines the harness entry point as `uv run python -m migratory.bench --workload <name> --backend <name>`, and slices 145 and 148 both use that form; that CLI has no `--config`, `--N`, `--ticks`, `--subdivision-factor`, or `--parity-check` flags, and no `scripts/bench.py` exists. Line 139's "draft demo script; it will be refined after implementation" leaves the primary verification artifact as a TBD. As written, none of A2, A3, A4, A5 has a runnable path. Rewrite against `-m migratory.bench` (the `mid-flock-50k` workload file already exists) and state where `S` and any ablation toggles enter — workload YAML field or CLI flag.

findings.title: Step 3's four-way ablation is two pairs of identical commands and needs an unspecified toggle — cut or specify it
findings.description: "Baseline (counter-gating)" and "Early exit only" are byte-identical (`--subdivision-factor 1 --ticks 200`), as are "Cell subdivision only" and "Both interventions" (`--subdivision-factor 3 --ticks 200`). No flag anywhere in the doc toggles the `break` on or off, and Intervention 1 *removes* counter-gating rather than preserving it behind a switch, so the baseline row cannot reproduce slice 145's ~38 TPS at all. The plan's exit criteria need only the recorded 145 baseline plus the S=3 gate run, so the four-way ablation is the heaviest option where a lighter one meets the requirement. Cut the two "only" rows and the "compose multiplicatively" quantification that depends on them, or specify one explicit early-exit toggle in the config surface and show it in the Component Interactions diagram. Do not ship four commands that produce two distinct measurements.

findings.title: A5's register-spill check prescribes tooling unavailable on the CUDA host
findings.description: A5 (line 124) requires "local memory per thread = 0 (confirmed via `nvcc --ptxas-info` or benchmark log)", and Step 4 says to look for `lmem` with "`TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1` or equivalent". Slice 148's Phase 2 envelope note records that `ptxas`, `cuobjdump`, and `nvcc` are **not installed** on the CUDA host (runtime driver only), and that slice verified no spill by counting `.local` declarations in the cached PTX and via `qd.profiler.print_kernel_profiler_info()`. "Or equivalent" is an implicit strategy, not an explicit handling rule. Name the concrete check that works on this host so A5 is actually verifiable.

findings.title: The slice plan's 7-neighbor benchmark target is silently dropped
findings.description: Plan 140 entry #10 assigns "the 7-neighbor operating point is a benchmark target" to this slice, and the 148 rediagnosis note makes the same point (`max_neighbors=7` is where counter-gating waste and early-exit gain are largest). The design fixes `max_neighbors=32` as the only gate configuration (line 128), never benchmarks 7, and does not defer it in Out of Scope. This is scope the plan assigns that the design drops without a decision. Add one 7-neighbor bench run to Step 3 (one extra command, no new mechanism), or move it into Out of Scope with a named follow-on.

findings.title: Parent NFR is restated with its specific target, and layer boundaries and dependency direction are correct
findings.description: Line 116 restates the parent NFR as "Tier 2 target is 60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA" with A2/A3 as measurable N=50k gates, satisfying the NFR-restatement requirement; A4 carries slice 145's 20% statistical-parity tolerance. CUDA-primary gating matches the architecture's "NVIDIA CUDA on Linux is the primary GPU substrate" goal, with Metal tuning explicitly out of scope, and the "profile before you optimize, profile after" principle is honored by the baseline-plus-gate runs. Dependency direction is 145 → 149 → 146 with no changes to `TickResult`, world-server wiring, numpy/numba backends, or agent state layout (lines 102–111) — keeping the tick return type contract as the sole engine/server boundary and keeping slice 146 unblocked. No new I/O paths or message types are introduced, so no additional failure-mode enumeration is due; the one new input (config `S`) is validated at config-load time with explicit `ValueError`s and no silent clamp (lines 70–78), consistent with the project's no-silent-fallback rule. The two-intervention scope otherwise fits the plan's Low risk / 2-of-5 effort rating.
